title: The structure of the LDL protein apoB100
summary: At the University of Missouri, Zachary Berndsen and Keith Cassidy used AlphaFold to predict the structure of apoB100, the scaffold of LDL particles, and refined it using cryo-electron microscopy data. The result is a cage-like shell with a ribbon belt. The post gives no figures such as resolution and no clinical validation.
organization: Google DeepMind and University of Missouri

evidence.tested: Cryo-EM images were refined with AlphaFold2 predictions; the resulting apoB100 structure was compared with more than 200 intramolecular cross-links and showed close agreement, with subnanometre resolution in most regions.
evidence.unknown: The article states that clinical applications will take time and the structure's implications are not yet realized; it gives no resolution figures or clinical validation, and the abstract states that resolution is subnanometre only in most regions.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold2 generated the initial atomic-resolution structure predictions, which were refined against cryo-EM data.
